feedback.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$-2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-8x+2y=13?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-8x+2y & =13 \\ {y}^{2}+2y-2{x}^{2}-8x & =13 \\ {y}^{2}+2y-2[{x}^{2}+4x] & =13 \\ (y+1)^{2}-1-2[(x+2)^{2}-4] & =13 \\ (y+1)^{2}-1-2(x+2)^{2}+8 & =13 \\ (y+1)^{2}-2(x+2)^{2} & =13+1-8 \\ (y+1)^{2}-2(x+2)^{2} & =6 \\ \frac{(y+1)^{2}}{6}-\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{3} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(-2,-1).$
